## Local gate loop (MCP image, Linux, isolated store clone), 2026-10-28 ~20:50 PDT

`rebar.llm.completion.verify_completion` called 3 times in one process. The model step did not run: the provider call failed with an Anthropic "Could not resolve authentication method" (the frontier class's `anthropic:` fallback), so the run covers precheck, pinned ticket view, store reads and tool setup, not the model turn.

| | RSS after (gc.collect) | GATE_PEAK_RSS delta |
|---|---|---|
| start | 36 MB | |
| run 1 | 385 MB | +231 MB |
| run 2 | 377 MB | +4.5 MB |
| run 3 | 392 MB | +3.6 MB |

So the non-model part of the gate retains about 350 MB after the first run and then stays flat. That is a one-time cost, not a per-run leak. It matches the first step on the box (60 MB → 544 MB after one job) to within the model-turn portion, which this run did not cover.

Still unexplained: the old container's stepwise climb to 2.68 GB (18:03–18:43 PDT) and the earlier 3.2 GB plateau. Hypotheses: (a) high-water retention, where concurrent gate jobs and reads each raise the peak and glibc keeps the freed pages; (b) a per-run leak in the model turn, which this run did not exercise. Next: watch the live container through its next gate jobs, recording anon memory against each job's start and end.
